log.msg: **`measure` — the population, not the statistic, and the module already owned every guard it was missing.** The band is `rules.js`'s `measure` rule read as a quantity, and it shipped with the rule's arithmetic and ONE of its three exemptions. Measured on `/framework/`: fourteen `p.page-preview-desc` captions supply **70 of 137 prose lines** at 160–188px and 19–26 characters, so the line-weighted median lands in them — and the rule's own comment has said `a card description, a table cell and a stat tile all run 18–24 legitimately` since it was written. The other half is worse and was never named: **a single 125px `td` running 13.7 characters over 8 lines WAS the whole reading of `styles/elements/misc/`**, and 17 `td` blocks supply 53 of 213 prose lines on `/framework/ui/` — while `rules.js` has exempted cells from this very measurement for months and `read.js`'s own `frame-gap` calls `in_cell()` twelve lines away. Population now: over 80 characters, not code, **not a cell, and not inside a frame** (its own box paints an edge or its parent's does — a card blurb, a chip, a stat tile). ⚠ Two candidate mechanisms were measured and REJECTED: a width-relative cluster (`the widest half of the prose`) reads captions on a page that has nothing else — `/notes/` fell to 24.1 — and a line-clamp guard throws away `/framework/ai/`'s genuine 258-character log lines at 3440, which are the real defect on that page.

**`scale` — BROKEN, and the proof is that it moves when you show it more of the SAME page.** The brief asked me to rule on whether `/framework/ui/` reading 11–12 was a defect or a correct reading of a page holding nineteen component demos. It is a defect, and not the one anyone guessed: the statistic — *how many 4px gap sizes cover four fifths of the page's gaps* — is **a function of how many gaps there are to look at**. Subsampled from one page's own gap population, `ext/Panel/` reads **7.6 → 11.0 → 10.0 → 13.8 → 15.2 → 17.0** at n = 25, 50, 100, 200, 400, 888; `styles/layouts/model/` reads 8.2 → 13.0 over the same sweep; every page tried roughly DOUBLES. Across 168 pages the reading ranks 0.551 (Spearman) with the gap count and 0.32 with the node count. So a big page scores badly for being big, which is exactly what `/framework/ui/` was doing. ⚠ The em-rendering hypothesis I went in with was WRONG and the data said so: bucketing each gap in quarter-ems of its container's font size instead of 4px moved the site median 5 → 6 at 1280 and 6 → 5 at 3440 — nothing. **The fix is to invert the statistic into its dual: the SHARE of the page's gaps that come from the four sizes it uses most.** Same question, and it converges: the same `ext/Panel/` sweep reads 0.74 → 0.66 → 0.61 → 0.61 → 0.60 → 0.58, flat from n=100. Both constants are inherited rather than fitted — FOUR is the top of the old ideal band (`2–4 is a scale someone chose`) and the 0.8 ideal floor is the old definition's own `four fifths`. ⚠ And the old band's low end was DEAD: `one gap is no hierarchy` never fired once, because the minimum reading across 168 pages at both widths was 2.00 and `ideal` began at 2.

**`contrast` — one line of population, and a character floor that had to be tried to be refuted.** On **165 of 169 pages the largest text is already a heading**, so `max(fs) ÷ median(fs)` is right almost everywhere and catastrophically wrong on the four rows where it is not: `/framework/` (a 125.7px `div.panel-t-time` clock, 8 characters, inside a Panel demo carrying no `data-layout-ignore`), `/framework/ui/` (the same shape — 18.20 at 3440), `styles/layouts/space/compose/` (an 86.4px framed `span`, 6 characters) and two pages whose largest text is smaller than their median. Numerator is now **the largest h1–h6**: max 8.38 → 3.92 at 1280 and 18.20 → 3.91 at 3440, out-of-range rows 2 → 1. ⚠ **The obvious fix is wrong and the numbers killed it in one run.** `the largest text with at least 12 characters` excludes the clock — and also excludes most of the site's page titles, because an `h1.page-title` runs 4–9 characters. It took the site median from 3.42 to **2.36** and the 25th percentile from 2.70 to **1.17**. A char-weighted 95th percentile was worse still (median 1.17). Length does not distinguish an ornament from a title; the TAG does. ⚠ A page with no heading now DECLINES rather than reading ~1.0 — `polish.js`'s `hierarchy` is the rule that reports a missing h1, and a band with no hierarchy to measure has nothing to say.

**THE SATURATION SWEEP, all eleven bands, 169 urls × 1280/3440, and it turns the `frame-gap` line into a census.** Full credit after the fixes, at 1280: `contrast` **163/165**, `width-used` **164/169**, `frame-gap` **138/141**, `lanes` 130/166, `depth` 105/166, `gap-share` 102/169, `pad-share` 80/139, `slivers` 64/155 (**142/155 at 3440**), `repetition` 59/166, `measure` 54/146, `scale` 48/168. Two of the four saturations are honest and say so in their own `why` — an app-shell page really does fill 1280, and nothing is a sliver at 3440 — and `contrast` measures the THEME (one type ramp, five discrete values across the whole corpus). **`frame-gap` is the one that was unexplained, and now is not: of the 141 pages that read it, 94 at 1280 and 93 at 3440 take their 10th percentile from OUTSIDE the content region, and 87 of those from THE SAME ELEMENT — `div.sidebar`, at exactly 1.400.** The next most repeated value is 0.89×17. Eighty-seven pages agreeing to three decimals is not a coincidence, it is one box. ⚠ **The other pattern the sweep found: three bands never reach either edge.** `pad-share`, `lanes` and `depth` record **zero hard zeros AND zero out-of-range rows at both widths** — they still taper, so they are not dead, but the outer half of each `ok` range has never been exercised by anything on this site and is untested rather than validated. None of the four is fixed: `frame-gap`'s repair is to read the content region like the six content bands, which takes it to null on every page with no framed content of its own, and the band keeps the root ON PURPOSE. That is Mike's call, not a subagent's.

**VERIFIED, and the tier's SPREAD grew while its mean stood still — which is the signature a re-derivation should have.** `tests/` — the 23 declared-verdict layouts — **23/23 at 400, 1280, 1920 and 3440**, so no rule with a written verdict moved in either direction. `taste/corpus/` reads **27 agree · 1 disagree · 14 n/a**, the same count tier-calibration recorded, and the per-case detail says nothing offset anything: `unbound the prose` still costs −0.67/−0.67/−0.27 on the three subjects it applies to, `pinned the body narrow` still costs a full −1 on all seven, and **`scrambled the spacing` — the case that exists for `scale` and is EXPECTED to fail — still reads +0 on all seven subjects, so the boundary it marks survives the new statistic.** The one disagreement is `took the padding out` on `pad-share · frame-gap`, neither of them a band I touched; ⚠ it has MOVED SUBJECT since the readme was written, from `gallery` to `split`, because `styles/layouts/space/presets.js` is rebuilt by other tasks — the readme now says to read the subject live along with the count. Tier-wide over 169 urls: **1280 mean 84.9 → 84.6, sd 7.60 → 8.71; 3440 mean 78.5 → 78.8, sd 9.29 → 9.84.** 16 of 16 module and subject pages load with zero console errors, zero failed requests and a rendered `.active-page`.

**SPOT-CHECKS against what the pages actually are.** `/framework/` — the front door, a card wall — `measure` **26.1 → 53.4** (its three `p.md` and eight `p` at 310–775px, which is what a reader reads there), `contrast` **8.38 → 3.01** (the 45.1px `h1` over the 15px body, instead of the 125.7px clock), `scale` 13 → 0.59, **taste 68 → 94 at both widths**. `/framework/ui/` — the page the `scale` question was asked about — 10–11 → **0.57–0.60**, so it is charged in proportion (credit 0.23–0.33) instead of taking a hard zero for holding nineteen demos; its `measure` 59.3 → 71.0 and its taste is unchanged at 85/90. `styles/elements/misc/` **13.7 → 48.0** (the 125px `td` gone), taste 82 → 95. **And two pages went DOWN, both correctly**: `/notes/git-branch-names/` declined to read `measure` at all before and now reads **89.3 characters** — real, hand-countable, and the page the vision baseline scored 78 while both tiers crowned it — taste 86 → 71; and `/framework/ai/` keeps its **258-character** log lines at 3440, which is the defect on that page and the reason a line-clamp guard was rejected. ⚠ `/notes/` still declines on `measure`: its only prose is two card captions, and a page with no reading column has nothing for this band to say.

**TWO CORRECTIONS TO THIS LOG ITSELF, both worth more than the lines they fix.** (1) **My earlier `at` timestamps run ahead of the wall clock** — I wrote 14:30 through 15:50 while the machine read 13:40 through 14:07.
